claims.object_mention: deficiency in the lysosomal enzyme galactocerebrosidase (GALC)
claims.quote: Krabbe disease (globoid cell leukodystrophy, GLD) is an inherited disease caused by a deficiency in the lysosomal enzyme galactocerebrosidase (GALC).
The major galactosylated lipid degraded by GALC is galactosylceramide.
However, GALC is also responsible for the degradation of galactosylsphingosine (psychosine), a highly cytotoxic glycolipid.

claims.object_mention: psychosine accumulation that kills oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells
claims.quote: It has been hypothesized that GALC-deficiency leads to psychosine accumulation that preferentially kills oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system and Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system.
Children affected with infantile Krabbe disease present with motor dysfunction, cognitive decline, intractable seizures, and premature death between two to five years of age.
